key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning produced the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks showed strong shared-task generalization.
engineering_relevance: The study helps weld-process engineers choose between a shared-representation model for efficient multi-target learning and a higher-accuracy ensemble for task-specific prediction.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding quality targets: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated both methods using RMSE and R² on the same dataset.
evidence_signal: Stacking ensemble achieved RMSE/R² of 0.0263/0.9863 for UTS, 0.0467/0.9782 for weld hardness, and 0.1109/0.8453 for HAZ hardness, outperforming MTNN on individual-task accuracy.
watch_item: Results may depend on dataset size and similarity among tasks, so stacking gains could reduce when data are sparse or when deployment requires simpler, more interpretable models.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
